interviewcake_second-largest-item-in-bst.incorrectReason: Assumes the maximum node has no left subtree; its predecessor may instead be the rightmost node of that subtree.

notes.explanation: Walk toward the largest key. If that node has a left subtree, its predecessor is the rightmost key in that subtree; otherwise its parent is the predecessor.
notes.correctness: A node's predecessor is the largest key in its left subtree, if that subtree exists. Otherwise it is the closest ancestor for which the node lies in the ancestor's right subtree. For the globally largest node this ancestor is its parent, so these cases identify exactly the greatest key remaining after the maximum is excluded.
notes.walkthrough: In the tree [12,5,20,2,9,17,25], the rightward search visits 12, 20 and 25. Node 25 has no left subtree, so its parent, 20, is the second-largest key. The tree remains unchanged.
edgeCases: largest node with a left branch
With two nodes, return the smaller key; if the maximum has a left subtree, use that subtree’s rightmost key rather than its parent.
notes.timeComplexity: O(h) time: the search follows a downward path to the maximum and at most another downward path in its left subtree, bounded by tree height h.
notes.spaceComplexity: O(1) auxiliary space: only the current node and its parent are retained; no traversal stack is built.

notes.correctness: Before each sale, the minimum contains precisely earlier prices. The best sale at that position uses that minimum; maximizing these candidates examines every legal pair implicitly.
notes.walkthrough: For prices [11,7,13,4,10], the first feasible profit is 7-11=-4. Price 7 becomes the cheapest earlier purchase; selling at 13 improves the profit to 6. The later low price 4 followed by 10 also gives 6. Updating the minimum only after considering a sale prevents buying and selling at the same position.

interviewcake_balanced-binary-tree.incorrectReason: Checks AVL-style local subtree heights instead of the specified deepest/shallowest LEAF depths; a one-leaf chain must be accepted.

notes.explanation: Traverse nodes with their depths, tracking the smallest and largest depths encountered at leaves. Reject once their difference exceeds one.
notes.correctness: The stored extremes are exactly the extrema among visited leaves. The final spread is the required global condition; an excessive partial spread can never decrease when more leaves are visited.
notes.walkthrough: For [4,2,7,1,3,null,9], the leaves are 1, 3 and 9. Each is two edges below the root, so the shallowest and deepest depths are both 2 and their difference is 0. Return true. A long chain would also return true because it has only one leaf.
edgeCases: leaf depths in separate subtrees. This is not per-node AVL height balance.
An empty tree returns true, and a chain of any supported length returns true because its only leaf supplies both depth extremes.
notes.timeComplexity: O(n) time: each of n nodes is pushed and visited at most once, with constant work per visit.
notes.spaceComplexity: O(h) auxiliary space: depth-first pending siblings occupy at most a constant number of entries per tree level; h can be n.

interviewcake_bst-checker.incorrectReason: Checks only immediate child ordering, missing violations of a more distant ancestor bound.

notes.explanation: Use a depth-first stack of nodes and open lower/upper bounds inherited from ancestors. The initial sentinels lie outside all signed 32-bit keys. Tighten the upper bound for a left child and the lower bound for a right child.
notes.correctness: Each bound summarizes every relevant ancestor restriction. Passing the current key as the new bound enforces all descendant restrictions inductively.
notes.walkthrough: For [10,4,16,1,7,12,19], node 4 inherits an upper bound of 10; its right child 7 must lie strictly between 4 and 10. Node 16 inherits a lower bound of 10, and its left child 12 must lie between 10 and 16. Every inherited interval is respected, so the answer is true.
edgeCases: A left descendant exceeding the root fails even if its immediate parent comparison succeeds; duplicate keys also fail. Signed 32-bit endpoints are valid keys.

interviewcake_bracket-validator.incorrectReason: Independent delimiter counts cannot detect crossed nesting such as ([)].

notes.explanation: Push openers onto a stack and compare each closer with the top. Reject a mismatch or an empty stack at a closer.
notes.correctness: The stack records exactly the unmatched openers in nesting order. A closer can legally match only the top, so each accepted match preserves the invariant.

edgeCases: Empty or delimiter-free input returns true; ([)] returns false because ) cannot close the top [.

interviewcake_linked-list-cycles.incorrectReason: Confuses equal node values with revisiting the same node identity, falsely rejecting acyclic repeated values.

notes.explanation: Move one pointer by one link and another by two. They meet exactly when a reachable cycle exists.
notes.correctness: Without a cycle the faster pointer reaches null. Within a cycle its relative position advances by one per iteration and eventually equals the slower pointer.
notes.walkthrough: For values [2,2,9] with tail link -1, the last node points to null. The repeated payload 2 does not imply a cycle: the two nodes are different objects. The fast pointer reaches the end, so return false. JSON supplies [listValues,tailLinkIndex]; -1 means a null tail. The callable receives only the constructed entry node and returns a boolean based on node identity.
edgeCases: An empty entry returns false. A node pointing to itself returns true; distinct nodes with equal values do not constitute a cycle.
notes.timeComplexity: O(n) time: an acyclic fast pointer reaches null after at most n links; after entering a cycle, the relative offset advances by one and meets within at most n more steps.

interviewcake_find-duplicate-files.incorrectReason: Groups files by length alone, falsely labeling equal-length files with different sampled bytes as duplicates.

notes.explanation: Group files by size and a fingerprint of at most 64 bytes each at the beginning, middle and end. For each matching pair, orient the paths by modification time.
notes.correctness: Equal fingerprints identify exactly the candidate groups defined by the adapter. Traversing every directory visits each file, and grouping retains enough information to emit each pair once without a full-content scan.
notes.walkthrough: The controlled directory contains a.txt and nested/b.txt, both with the bytes "same bytes". Their sizes and all three bounded samples match. Their modification times are 1000 and 2000, so report their full paths with a.txt first as the earlier-time candidate. This orientation is a heuristic, and equal fingerprints can still be false positives; neither file is changed. JSON supplies controlled file descriptors. The callable receives the temporary directory’s full path and returns FilePaths pairs containing full paths; displayed expected paths are relative to that directory.
edgeCases: deliberate sample collisions. No file deletion or writes.
Empty directories return no pairs. Two empty files have identical fingerprints; equal timestamps permit either orientation. Matching sampled bytes do not prove equal complete content.

notes.spaceComplexity: O(f) bounded fingerprints plus stored path characters and directory traversal state; returned pairs add path storage. The bound is independent of total file-content bytes.

interviewcake_find-duplicate-optimize-fo.incorrectReason: Treats a prefix exactly at capacity as overcrowded, steering toward a value that may occur only once.

notes.explanation: Bisect candidate values using the count C(m) of all entries at most midpoint m, comparing that count with the m available values in 1..m. Keep the half whose endpoint counts still bracket excess population.
notes.correctness: Maintain C(lower-1)<=lower-1 and C(upper)>upper. Initially C(0)=0 and C(n)=n+1. If C(mid)>mid, set upper=mid; otherwise set lower=mid+1. At the final value v, C(v)>v and C(v-1)<=v-1, so their difference, the number of v entries, is at least two. This argument does not assume that C(m)>m is monotone.
notes.walkthrough: For [1,3,4,2,3], lower=1 and upper=4. At midpoint 2, C(2)=2, so lower becomes 3. At midpoint 3, C(3)=4>3, so upper becomes 3. Return 3. Counts cover the whole prefix 1..midpoint, not just the current interval; the endpoint invariant guarantees that the final value repeats.
edgeCases: [1,1] returns 1 without a counting pass. Multiple repeated values are allowed; any actual duplicate passes.
notes.timeComplexity: O(n log n) time: halving the n-value search interval takes O(log n) rounds, each scanning all n+1 entries.
notes.spaceComplexity: O(1) auxiliary space: interval endpoints, midpoint and count only; input is read-only.
notes.attribution: Original EPI Practice implementation and explanation. Task identity and technical compatibility facts are attributed to Interview Cake; no course prose, examples, solution code or artwork are included. No affiliation is implied.

interviewcake_find-duplicate-optimize-fo.incorrectReason: Returns the cycle entry successor instead of its index; that successor need not be a duplicated value.

notes.explanation: View each array entry as the next-index pointer. Run Floyd’s slow/fast search starting at numbers[0], then reset slow to that same start and advance both one step to the cycle entry.
notes.correctness: The path from index 0 enters a cycle because all links are in 1..n, excluding 0. Its entry has two distinct incoming source indices: the path predecessor and the cycle predecessor. Starting Floyd at numbers[0] removes the first path edge but preserves this entry (or starts directly on it). At a meeting, the faster walker has gained whole cycle lengths; resetting one walker to the chosen start makes equal-speed walkers meet at the entry.
notes.walkthrough: For [4,1,3,4,2], start both walkers at numbers[0]=4. After successive moves (slow,fast) is (2,3), (3,2), then (4,4). Reset slow to 4; the walkers already agree, so return 4. In the full path 0 -> 4 -> 2 -> 3 -> 4, indices 0 and 3 both point to 4, proving it is repeated.
edgeCases: [1,1] returns 1; other valid inputs may contain several duplicate values, so no particular duplicate is mandated.
notes.timeComplexity: O(n) time: Floyd’s meeting phase traverses a prefix and cycle of at most n+1 indices; the entry phase takes at most the prefix length.
notes.spaceComplexity: O(1) auxiliary space: a fixed number of index walkers, with no copied array or visited set.

interviewcake_find-rotation-point.incorrectReason: Returns a one-based position even though the specified rotation index is zero-based.

notes.explanation: Compare the middle word with the right boundary. The smallest word remains in the half containing the ordering break, or at the middle boundary.

interviewcake_graph-coloring.incorrectReason: Compares palette colors with neighbor labels instead of assigned colors, permitting adjacent equal colors.

notes.explanation: For each node, collect colors already used by its neighbors and choose a palette color outside that set.

notes.walkthrough: For the triangle with adjacency [[1,2],[0,2],[0,1]] and palette [red,blue,green], assign red to v0, blue to v1 because v0 is red, and green to v2 because its neighbors use both red and blue. Every edge has different endpoint colors. Any other valid assignment also passes; the displayed true reports successful properties. JSON supplies [adjacency,palette]; the callable receives graph nodes and colors and returns void/None/undefined. Expected true is the checker verdict for legal Color mutations and preserved graph identity/links.
edgeCases: An empty graph needs no assignments. Isolated nodes can all use the first color. A clique of D+1 nodes uses D+1 distinct colors.

interviewcake_highest-product-of-3.incorrectReason: Taking only the three largest values misses two large-magnitude negative values whose product is positive.

notes.explanation: Track the largest and smallest one-value and two-value products while scanning. Each new value can extend either extreme two-value product to a three-value candidate.

interviewcake_queue-two-stacks.incorrectReason: Implements LIFO removal rather than FIFO order when several enqueued items remain.

notes.explanation: Push new items to an input stack. When the output stack is empty, transfer all input items into it; this reverses their order once.
notes.correctness: The output stack top is always the oldest remaining item. Transfer is performed only when it is empty, so newer items never pass older ones. Each item is moved at most once.
notes.walkthrough: Enqueue 4 and 9 into the incoming stack. The first Dequeue moves them to the outgoing stack and removes 4. Enqueue 2 without moving the still-pending 9. The next Dequeue removes 9; only then does transferring the incoming stack expose 2. The returned values are 4, 9 and 2 in FIFO order. JSON supplies [operationNames,argumentLists] for one fresh QueueTwoStacks. Void operations display null; Dequeue displays the returned item or {"error":"empty"}.
edgeCases: Dequeue on a fresh or drained queue throws an empty-state exception, normalized to {"error":"empty"}; duplicate values remain separate occurrences.
notes.timeComplexity: O(1) amortized per operation: each item is pushed to incoming, transferred once, then popped from outgoing. A single transfer-triggering Dequeue can cost O(q); m operations cost O(m).
notes.spaceComplexity: O(q) persistent space: each of q queued occurrences lives in exactly one of the two stacks.

interviewcake_shuffle.incorrectReason: Swapping each slot with an unrestricted random slot is biased: for three distinct entries, 27 equal-probability choice streams cannot distribute equally over six permutations.

interviewcake_mesh-message.incorrectReason: Returns an empty route instead of the explicitly required null when the endpoints are disconnected.

notes.explanation: Breadth-first search records the predecessor of each first-discovered vertex. Reconstruct the route backward from the destination.
notes.correctness: BFS discovers vertices in nondecreasing distance from start. A predecessor chain from first discovery therefore has minimum edge count; the visited set prevents cycling.
notes.walkthrough: In the network a:{b,c}, b:{a,d}, c:{a,d}, d:{b,c}, breadth-first search visits b and c at distance 1 and discovers d at distance 2. Reconstructing via b gives [a,b,d]. The equally short route [a,c,d] is also valid; both contain two edges. JSON supplies an adjacency map and two endpoint labels. Return any shortest route including endpoints; the adapter accepts tied routes and a no-route result.
edgeCases: start=end returns [start]. A disconnected destination returns no route; tied shortest paths may use different valid predecessor choices.
notes.timeComplexity: Expected O(V+E) time: each discovered vertex is enqueued once and each outgoing adjacency entry examined at most once; reconstruction visits at most V predecessors. Labels are treated as bounded-size hash keys.
notes.spaceComplexity: O(V) auxiliary space for the queue and predecessor map, plus an O(V) result route.

interviewcake_compress-url-list.incorrectReason: Confuses an existing prefix path with an inserted complete word; first insertion of a prefix or the empty key incorrectly reports false.

notes.explanation: Store a trie edge per next character and an explicit terminal flag at complete keys.
notes.correctness: The path represents a key's exact characters. Only its terminal flag denotes complete-key membership, so shared prefixes never create false complete keys.
notes.walkthrough: Insert https://a/b: create missing character links and mark its final node, returning true. Insert https://a next: its character path exists, but its final node was not a complete key, so return true. Repeating https://a/b returns false. Extending it to https://a/b/c marks a different complete key and returns true. JSON supplies [operationNames,argumentLists] for one fresh Trie. Each AddWord receives one exact string and returns whether that complete key was newly inserted.

The empty key marks the root and returns true once, then false. Inserting a shorter prefix after a longer key returns true if its terminal marker was unset.
notes.timeComplexity: Expected O(L+1) time per insertion: follow or create one hash-map edge per character of a length-L key, then inspect its terminal marker.

interviewcake_matching-parens.incorrectReason: Returns the first closing parenthesis, ignoring nested pairs that must close before the supplied opener.

notes.explanation: Scan starting at the designated opening parenthesis, including it in the depth count. Increment for each opener and decrement for each closer; the first decrement to zero identifies its matching closer.
notes.correctness: After consuming the designated opener, depth counts the still-unclosed openers within that outer pair, including the outer opener itself. Nested pairs increase and then decrease this count. The first return to zero therefore closes the designated opener rather than an inner pair.
notes.walkthrough: In x(ab(cd)e)y, the opener at index 1 starts depth 1. The opener at index 4 increases depth to 2, its closer at index 7 reduces it to 1, and the closer at index 9 reduces it to 0. Return index 9 rather than the first closing parenthesis.
edgeCases: An adjacent () returns the next index; nested pairs must close before the designated pair. The bank guarantees that a matching closer exists.
notes.timeComplexity: O(n) worst-case time: scan forward from the supplied opener until its match, visiting each intervening character once.
notes.spaceComplexity: O(1) auxiliary space: an integer depth replaces a stack because only one bracket type matters.

interviewcake_permutation-palindrome.incorrectReason: Rejects every valid odd-length palindrome multiset with its permitted single odd-frequency center.

notes.explanation: Toggle each letter in a set of odd-frequency letters. A palindrome permits at most one odd frequency.
notes.correctness: Mirrored positions use characters in pairs, leaving at most one center occurrence. Conversely, pairing each even part and placing the possible odd remainder at the center constructs a palindrome.
notes.walkthrough: For aabbc, toggling odd-frequency membership removes a after its second occurrence and removes b after its second. Only c remains odd. It can occupy the middle of a palindrome such as abcba, so return true without enumerating reorderings.
edgeCases: The empty string is a palindrome permutation. aabc returns false because both b and c have odd counts.
notes.timeComplexity: O(n) time: each of n letters toggles one parity and the final odd count is checked.
notes.spaceComplexity: O(1) auxiliary space for the fixed 26-letter domain, except a language implementation that copies the input characters as noted below.

interviewcake_product-of-other-numbers.incorrectReason: The division shortcut fails on zero entries and violates the required division-free approach.

notes.explanation: Write left-prefix products into the output, then multiply them by a running right-suffix product while scanning backward.
notes.correctness: Before the reverse scan, output[i] contains precisely factors left of i. The suffix contains precisely factors right of i, so multiplying them excludes exactly the required position.
notes.walkthrough: For [2,0,-3,4], the left-product pass writes [1,2,0,0]. Multiplying right products into those entries gives [0,-24,0,0]. At the zero position, the other values multiply to 2*(-3)*4=-24; every other position includes the zero. Division is unnecessary.
edgeCases: One zero leaves only its own result potentially nonzero; two zeros make every result zero. No division or special zero branch is needed.
notes.timeComplexity: O(n) time: two passes each perform a constant number of multiplications per position.
notes.spaceComplexity: O(n) result storage and O(1) additional auxiliary space: only running prefix/suffix products and indices.

interviewcake_rectangular-love.incorrectReason: Treats boundary contact as an area intersection instead of returning the required all-zero no-overlap rectangle.

notes.explanation: Intersect the x intervals and y intervals separately. Both resulting lengths must be positive.
notes.correctness: A coordinate belongs to the overlap exactly when it lies in both corresponding intervals. Their common lower endpoint is the maximum lower endpoint and their upper endpoint is the minimum upper endpoint.
notes.walkthrough: Rectangle [1,2,6,4] spans x=1..7 and y=2..6; [4,0,5,4] spans x=4..9 and y=0..4. The common x interval is 4..7 and the common y interval is 2..4, so return a new rectangle [4,2,3,2]. Both dimensions are positive. JSON rectangles are [LeftX,BottomY,Width,Height]; return a new Rectangle, including [0,0,0,0] when overlap has no positive area.
edgeCases: Edge or corner contact returns a new [0,0,0,0] rectangle because at least one overlap dimension is zero. Containment returns the smaller rectangle’s geometry in a fresh object.
notes.timeComplexity: O(1) time: four endpoint comparisons and at most two subtractions determine the intersection.
notes.spaceComplexity: O(1) auxiliary and result space: a fixed number of coordinates and one new Rectangle.

interviewcake_recursive-string-permutati.incorrectReason: Omits the empty string permutation, although the empty input has one valid permutation rather than zero.

notes.explanation: Count each distinct character, then recursively extend a prefix with any character whose remaining count is positive. Decrement before recursion and restore after it so sibling choices see the original counts.
notes.correctness: Each recursive state has used exactly the prefix multiset and retains exactly the unused occurrences. Choosing a positive-count character preserves this invariant; reaching full length uses every occurrence. Every distinct target string determines one available next-character choice at each level, so all and only distinct permutations are reached.
notes.walkthrough: For ab, counts start as {a:1,b:1}. Choose a, leaving only b and emitting ab; restore the counts. Choose b, leaving only a and emitting ba. For aa, there is only one available character choice at either level, so aa is emitted once. Empty input immediately emits the empty string. Return a set of strings; the adapter displays a JSON array and compares membership without imposing output order.
edgeCases: repeated characters under the bank extension.
Empty input returns the singleton set {""}; repeated characters yield distinct strings only, not repeated output entries.
notes.timeComplexity: Expected O(n*n!) worst-case time: with distinct characters there are n! output strings, each constructed/hashed in O(n); all smaller recursion levels are dominated by this bound.
notes.spaceComplexity: O(n*n!) worst-case output storage. Outside the output, the count map and recursion depth are O(n); immutable prefixes retained along a recursion path can total O(n²) characters.

interviewcake_reverse-linked-list.incorrectReason: Returns reversed values in newly allocated nodes instead of reversing the required original objects and links.

notes.explanation: Maintain the already reversed prefix and detach one node at a time from the remaining suffix, pointing it back to the prefix.
notes.correctness: The prefix always contains the original first nodes in reverse order, and the suffix is untouched. Moving its first node extends the invariant until no suffix remains.
notes.walkthrough: For nodes 3 -> 8 -> 1, first set node 3.Next to null. Next point the original node 8 to node 3, then point the original node 1 to node 8. Return the original node holding 1. The resulting values are [1,8,3], with every payload still attached to its original object. The callable returns the new head of the same node objects. JSON displays the returned head’s value sequence; the adapter also checks original identities, payloads and reversed links.
edgeCases: Empty input returns null; a singleton returns the same object. The old head becomes the tail with Next=null, even when payload values repeat.
notes.timeComplexity: O(n) time: each of n nodes has its Next link rewritten once.
notes.spaceComplexity: O(1) auxiliary space: current, saved next and previous references; no replacement nodes.

interviewcake_reverse-string-in-place.incorrectReason: Reverses a copy and rebinds the local parameter, leaving the caller-owned mutable character array unchanged.

notes.explanation: Swap the leftmost and rightmost unprocessed characters, moving both boundaries inward.
notes.correctness: Each swap places both boundary characters at their final reversed positions. The remaining middle interval is the same problem on fewer characters.
notes.walkthrough: For the mutable characters of cloud, exchange c with d, then l with u; the middle o stays in place. The same array now contains duolc. No replacement array is returned. JSON encodes the mutable character array as one string. The callable returns void/None/undefined; expected is the same array’s content after mutation.
edgeCases: Empty and singleton arrays retain their identity and content. An odd-length center character stays unchanged.
notes.timeComplexity: O(n) time: each inward swap fixes two characters, with at most ceil(n/2) swaps.
notes.spaceComplexity: O(1) auxiliary space: two indices and a swap temporary; no new character buffer.

interviewcake_reverse-words.incorrectReason: Reverses the entire message but forgets to restore the internal character order of each word.

notes.explanation: Reverse the entire character array, then reverse the characters of each resulting word.
notes.correctness: The first reversal reverses word order and each word's letters. Reversing each word restores its spelling while leaving the new word order intact.
notes.walkthrough: For foxes run fast, reversing all characters gives tsaf nur sexof. Reverse each space-delimited segment in that same array to restore the internal spelling, producing fast run foxes. Spaces remain separators and the array length is unchanged. JSON encodes the mutable character array as one string. The callable returns void/None/undefined; expected is the same array’s word-reversed content.
edgeCases: Empty input stays empty. A single word is reversed twice and finishes unchanged; unequal word lengths need no extra storage.
notes.timeComplexity: O(n) time: one full reversal, one boundary scan, and word reversals whose total lengths sum to at most n.
notes.spaceComplexity: O(1) auxiliary space: all reversals swap within the original mutable character array; only range indices are stored.

interviewcake_simulate-5-sided-die.incorrectReason: Modulo maps seven equally likely draws onto five outcomes unevenly instead of rejecting source values 6 and 7.

notes.explanation: Reject source outcomes 6 and 7; return every remaining outcome unchanged.
notes.correctness: Each accepted source value has the same probability 1/7. Conditioning on acceptance gives probability 1/5 for each result; repeated independent attempts preserve that distribution.
notes.walkthrough: With injected draws 6, 7, 3, reject 6 and 7 and return 3. In general each accepted source value 1..5 has the same source probability, so conditioning on acceptance gives probability 1/5. The judge output true denotes passed range, source-use and probability properties, not a fixed rolled value. Rand5 has no value arguments and returns one integer 1..5. JSON contains a judge-only forced Rand7 draw prefix; expected true denotes random-source/range/distribution checks, not the rolled integer.
edgeCases: do not map rejected outcomes modulo five.
Any number of 6/7 draws must be rejected; returning draw modulo five would bias outcomes. Every call uses fresh supplied randomness.
notes.timeComplexity: Expected O(1) time: each attempt succeeds with probability 5/7, so the expected number of source calls is 7/5. There is no finite worst-case call bound.
notes.spaceComplexity: O(1) auxiliary space: retain only the current draw, regardless of the number of rejected attempts.

interviewcake_simulate-7-sided-die.incorrectReason: Skips rejection of the last four draw pairs, giving some output faces four preimages and others only three.

notes.explanation: Combine two zero-based source draws into a uniform state in 0..24. Accept states below 21 and map each group of seven uniformly into 1..7.
notes.correctness: Each pair is one of 25 equally likely states. Accepting 21 states leaves three representatives for each remainder modulo seven, so each result has conditional probability 1/7.
notes.walkthrough: For injected draws 5,5,1,1, the first pair creates state (5-1)*5+(5-1)=24, which is rejected. The next pair creates state 0 and returns 1. Among accepted states 0..20, each remainder modulo seven occurs three times, giving probability 1/7 for each output. The displayed true reports the judge properties. Rand7 has no value arguments and returns one integer 1..7. JSON contains a judge-only forced Rand5 draw prefix; expected true denotes random-source/range/distribution checks, not the rolled integer.
edgeCases: no modulo bias from all 25 states.
States 21..24 must be rejected; taking all 25 states modulo seven would favor four outcomes. Repeated rejections must not cache a previous roll.
notes.timeComplexity: Expected O(1) time: an attempt succeeds with probability 21/25 and uses two source calls, for 50/21 expected calls. Worst-case attempts are unbounded.
notes.spaceComplexity: O(1) auxiliary space: two draws and one encoded state, reused on every retry.

interviewcake_temperature-tracker.incorrectReason: Truncates nonintegral means even though GetMean must preserve the arithmetic fractional result.

notes.explanation: Keep a fixed 111-entry frequency table, running sum/count and cached extrema/mode. Each insertion updates these constant-size statistics.
notes.correctness: The frequency table counts every insertion. Extrema are updated against every new value; sum/count define the mean; updating the mode on a new largest frequency preserves a maximizing value.
notes.walkthrough: Insert 4, 10 and 4. The minimum is 4, maximum 10, sum 18 and count 3, so the mean is 6. Frequency 4 is 2 while frequency 10 is 1, so GetMode returns 4. Repeating getters does not consume any reading. JSON supplies [operationNames,argumentLists] for one fresh TempTracker. Insert displays null; empty getters return null, means allow 1e-9 tolerance and any maximizing mode is valid.
edgeCases: Empty getters return null. With readings 3 and 8, either mode is accepted; means use floating-point division and getters do not consume readings.
notes.timeComplexity: O(1) per insertion/getter: insertion changes one frequency bucket and a fixed number of cached statistics; getters read cached values.
notes.spaceComplexity: O(1) persistent space: exactly 111 frequency slots plus count, sum, extrema and mode, independent of reading count.

interviewcake_cake-thief.incorrectReason: Uses a descending 0/1-knapsack update, allowing each cake type only once instead of an unbounded number of whole items.

notes.explanation: First detect an unbounded zero-weight type. Otherwise compute the best value for each capacity by considering the last positive-weight item selected.
notes.correctness: For a bounded instance, an optimal nonempty selection has a final positive-weight item. Removing it leaves a feasible selection at the remaining capacity, so maximizing all such choices establishes the recurrence by induction.
notes.walkthrough: For types [weight=3,value=7] and [weight=5,value=13] with capacity 11, choose one weight-5 item and two weight-3 items. Total weight is 11 and value is 13+7+7=27. Two weight-5 items yield only 26; three weight-3 items yield 21. The unbounded dynamic program reuses earlier capacity optima to find 27.
edgeCases: Any zero-weight positive-value type raises InfinityException even when capacity is zero. Zero-weight zero-value types are ignored; empty types produce value 0.
notes.timeComplexity: O(t*C+t+C+1) time: inspect t types for infinity, initialize C+1 cells, and test every type for each capacity 1..C.
notes.spaceComplexity: O(C+1) auxiliary space: one best value per capacity, with no table indexed by item counts.

interviewcake_find-unique-int-among-dupl.incorrectReason: Reverses the sign in the distinct-sum identity, returning the negative of the unique positive ID.

notes.explanation: XOR all values. Each duplicated value cancels itself, leaving the unmatched one.
notes.correctness: XOR is associative and commutative, and x XOR x is zero. Paired values therefore cancel regardless of ordering, leaving the unique value.
notes.walkthrough: For [14,3,14,8,3], XOR combines equal pairs to zero: 14^14=0 and 3^3=0. Since XOR is associative and commutative, the final accumulator equals 8, the only identifier without a cancelling partner.
edgeCases: A singleton returns its value. Large or nonconsecutive IDs need no range-indexed storage; the exact once/twice multiplicity promise is essential.
notes.timeComplexity: O(n) time: perform one XOR per input entry.
notes.spaceComplexity: O(1) auxiliary space: a single XOR accumulator and iteration state.

interviewcake_top-scores.incorrectReason: Emits the counting-sort buckets in ascending order instead of the requested nonincreasing order.

notes.explanation: Count occurrences in K+1 buckets, then emit each bucket from K down to zero.
notes.correctness: Each input occurrence increments exactly its score bucket. Emitting buckets in decreasing score order preserves multiplicity and produces the required ordering.
notes.walkthrough: For scores [3,8,3,0,5] and K=8, the count table records one 8, one 5, two 3s and one 0. Reading counts from score 8 down to 0 emits [8,5,3,3,0] in a new array. Both occurrences of 3 are retained.
edgeCases: K=0 permits only zeros, all retained; empty scores yield an empty new array even if K is positive.
notes.timeComplexity: O(n+K+1) time: initialize and scan K+1 buckets, count n entries, then emit exactly n occurrences.
notes.spaceComplexity: O(K+1) auxiliary count storage plus O(n) for the new output array.

interviewcake_which-appears-twice.incorrectReason: Omits the largest domain value from the XOR cancellation loop, an off-by-one error that changes the duplicated value.

notes.explanation: XOR every array entry, then XOR every integer in the promised range 1..n. Each required occurrence cancels its matching range occurrence, leaving the extra value.
notes.correctness: Associativity and commutativity let matching values cancel because x XOR x=0. The input is exactly the range multiset plus one extra occurrence, so cancellation leaves that occurrence. No large sum or multiplication is formed.
notes.walkthrough: For [3,1,4,2,3], XOR the input values, then XOR 1,2,3,4 because n=4. One copy of every required value cancels its range partner; the extra 3 remains, so return 3. The algorithm uses XOR rather than a sum formula.

notes.timeComplexity: O(n) time: process the n+1 input entries; the range sum is constant-time arithmetic, or an additional n XOR operations in the XOR variants.
notes.spaceComplexity: O(1) auxiliary space: scalar accumulator and range/loop variables, with no input mutation.

interviewcake_word-cloud.incorrectReason: Drops internal apostrophes and hyphens, splitting valid bank words such as contractions and hyphenated compounds.

notes.explanation: Find all maximal tokens with the pattern [A-Za-z]+(?:['-][A-Za-z]+)*, lowercase each match, and increment its key in a null-prototype dictionary. The pattern permits a hyphen/apostrophe only between letter runs, and a null prototype keeps words such as constructor from colliding with inherited properties.
notes.correctness: The expression starts each token with at least one letter and extends it only through another letter block joined by one allowed connector. Each maximal token under the disclosed grammar is therefore matched once; separators are excluded. Lowercasing sends all permitted case variants to the same key, and one increment per match records exactly their occurrence count.
notes.walkthrough: For "Owls fly; OWLS don't crawl. Fly-by owls!", punctuation ends tokens but internal apostrophes and letter-surrounded hyphens remain. Lowercasing combines Owls, OWLS and owls into count 3. The other keys are fly, don't, crawl and fly-by, each counted once under the disclosed bank policy. Construct WordCloudData from the input string and inspect WordsToCounts; the displayed dictionary is the exposed property, not a constructor return value. Dictionary order is irrelevant.
edgeCases: Empty text yields an empty dictionary. red--blue splits into red and blue; a letter-surrounded apostrophe or single hyphen remains inside a token.
notes.timeComplexity: Expected O(n) time: tokenization, lowercase conversion and hashing examine O(n) total characters. The dictionary performs one expected constant-time update per token after hashing.
notes.spaceComplexity: O(n) worst-case space: input.match materializes all matched tokens, and the result dictionary stores distinct normalized keys and counts.
